classes.name: AdministrationPage
classes.description:
# Page Description
The Administration overview at `/admin`: a grid of tiles, one per
administration area. Only administrators can open it; it is reached from
the header's user menu via {@link GlobalHeaderComp.clickAdministrationLink}.

methods.name: clickUsersAndPermissionsTile
methods.description: Opens the users list from the "Users and permissions" tile.
methods.prerequisites: The Administration overview is open and the user is an administrator
methods.observableState: The browser navigates to /users, the list of every user account

classes.name: AdminUsersPage
classes.description:
# Page Description
The administration list of user accounts at `/users`, with a filter panel
(Status, Name) above the table. Administrators only.

Not to be confused with a project's Members page ({@link MembersPage}),
which lists the users *of one project*: this lists every account.

methods.name: filterByName
methods.description:
Filters the list by name and returns the reloaded list.

The filter is a `GET` form, so applying navigates; the wait is on a
non-empty `name=` in the URL, because `waitForLoadState('load')` would
resolve against the document still on screen (the same trap as
{@link MembersPage.filterByName}). The filter matches login, first
name, last name and email.
methods.observableState: The table reloads showing only users matching the name; the URL carries `name`

methods.name: clickUserByLogin
methods.description:
Opens a user's edit page from the Username column.

The link's text is the user's **login** (which, for a user created
through {@link NewUserPage}, is their email), and for an administrator it
leads to the edit page (`allowed_management_user_profile_path`,
`app/helpers/users_helper.rb:144`). Filter first with
{@link filterByName} — the list is paginated.
methods.prerequisites: The users list is open and shows the user

classes.name: EditUserPage
classes.description:
# Page Description
The administrator's edit page for one user, `/users/<id>/edit`, on its
General tab: the user's attributes, an Authentication section with the
password fields, and status actions (Send invitation, Lock permanently /
Unlock) in the page header.

Users cannot be deleted on this instance (`users_deletable_by_admins` is
off, so the header renders no Delete action); locking is how a test retires
a user it created.

methods.name: setPassword
methods.description:
Sets the user's password: fills Password and Confirmation and saves.

Setting a password **activates an invited user**
(`users_controller.rb:107-116`), which is what makes a user created
through {@link NewUserPage} able to sign in. The save redirects back to
this page; the "Lock permanently" action appearing is what marks the
reloaded page, because it is only offered for an active user.

The password must meet the instance's rules — on this one, at least 10
characters.
methods.prerequisites: The edit page of a user with internal authentication is open
methods.observableState: The user has the password, its status is active, and "Lock permanently" is offered

methods.name: lockPermanently
methods.description:
Locks the user permanently, so the account can no longer sign in. The
header then offers "Unlock" in its place.
methods.prerequisites: The edit page of an active user is open, and it is not the signed-in administrator's own
methods.observableState: The user's status is locked and "Unlock" is offered

classes.name: NewUserPage
classes.description:
# Page Description
The administrator's New user form at `/users/new`
(`app/views/users/new.html.erb`).

It asks only for a name and an email: **there is no password field**. The
account is created with status *invited* and its login set to the email
(`users_controller.rb:309-314`), and creating it lands on the user's edit
page — where {@link EditUserPage.setPassword} gives it a password and, by
doing so, activates it.

methods.name: fillFirstName
methods.prerequisites: The New user form is open
methods.observableState: The First name field holds the text; nothing is saved until {@link clickCreateButton}

methods.name: fillLastName
methods.prerequisites: The New user form is open
methods.observableState: The Last name field holds the text; nothing is saved until {@link clickCreateButton}

methods.name: fillEmail
methods.description: Fills the Email field. The new user's login defaults to this address.
methods.prerequisites: The New user form is open
methods.observableState: The Email field holds the text; nothing is saved until {@link clickCreateButton}

methods.name: clickCreateButton
methods.description:
Submits the form with "Create". On success the server redirects to the
new user's edit page (`users_controller.rb:96`); an invalid submission
re-renders the form at `/users`, so waiting for the edit page also fails
fast on a rejected user.
methods.prerequisites: First name, last name and email are filled
methods.observableState: The user exists with status invited, and the browser shows /users/<id>/edit

methods.name: createUser
methods.signature: createUser(firstName: string, lastName: string, email: string): Promise<EditUserPage>
methods.description:
Creates a user end to end: fills the name and email and submits. Use the
individual fill methods when a test needs to observe the form itself.
methods.prerequisites: The New user form is open
methods.observableState: The user exists with status invited and login equal to the email; the browser shows its edit page
